turns.text: I was just started on methotrexate tablets for my rheumatoid arthritis and the label says 'once weekly'. What should I know about taking it properly as a new patient?
Why is it taken weekly when all my other tablets are daily? How does it work differently?
Is there a best day or time to take it, and does it matter whether it's with food?
What do rheumatology nurses usually tell people in the first month? I'd like to be doing what they'd expect.
What blood tests will the clinic want and how often? What are they checking for?
Someone in an online forum said folic acid on the other days made a big difference to side effects. Is that standard?
A friend with arthritis said it took her three months to notice anything. Is that normal, and what should I expect week by week?
My joints are so bad I can't open jars and the clinic can't see me for three months. What can I do for the pain meanwhile without touching the methotrexate?
I'm nervous about side effects. Which ones are normal and which mean I should call someone straight away?
Could you write me a simple weekly routine — the weekly dose, folic acid, pain relief, what to track — until the clinic sees me?
